title: WRITE IT WHERE YOU CAN SEE IT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people: 'Keep all these commands that I give you today. When you have crossed the Jordan into the land the Lord your God is giving you, set up some large stones and coat them with plaster.'" — Deut 27:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As Israel prepared to enter the promised land, God gave an unusual instruction. The moment they crossed the Jordan, they were to set up large stones, coat them with plaster, and write God's words on them for all to see. Before they built houses, before they planted fields, they were to make God's Word visible and central.

There is wisdom here for us. It is so easy to let God's Word slip to the edges of a busy life. We mean to read it, to remember it, but the days fill up and it fades into the background. Israel was told to make the Word unmissable — literally written in plain sight at the entrance to their new life.

What would it look like for you to "write God's Word where you can see it"? A verse on your wall, a reminder on your phone, Scripture spoken over your children, a habit of opening the Bible before the day swallows you. The point is not decoration; it is keeping God's truth in front of your eyes and heart so it shapes everything that follows.

The Word we treasure ultimately points us to Christ, the living Word (John 1:14). Keeping Scripture visible keeps Him central. As you begin anything new, let God's Word go first.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where has God's Word drifted to the edges of my daily life?
2. What is one practical way I can keep Scripture in front of me this week?
3. Does God's truth shape my decisions, or only decorate my walls?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me keep Your Word central and visible in my life, not pushed to the edges. Let Your truth shape everything I do. Amen.
